title: Carrier-assisted One-pot Sample Preparation for Targeted Proteomics Analysis of Small Numbers of Human Cells

We are working on several different ways to further improve cLC-SRM performance with the potential of moving towards sensitive targeted single-cell proteomics. When compared to other MS-based single-cell proteomics methods that require specific devices, cLC-SRM can be readily implemented in any MS proteomics laboratory without additional investment on specific devices for sample processing. But it can only be used for quantitative analysis of target proteins of interest. Unlike global single-cell proteomics methods for relative untargeted quantification, cLC-SRM can provide accurate or absolute quantification of target proteins in small numbers of cells including single cells. Furthermore, cLC-SRM has significant advantages over conventional targeted single-cell proteomics using antibody-based immunoassays in terms of multiplexing and quantitation specificity and accuracy. Future developments will focus on significant improvements in detection sensitivity and sample throughput for enabling rapid absolute quantification of most proteins (e.g., important negative feedback regulators) in single human cells. Automation of cLC-SRM is another direction to improve its robustness, reproducibility, and the overall sample throughput with commercially available liquid handlers. We anticipate that cLC-SRM will be broadly used for multiplexed accurate quantification of target proteins in small subpopulations of cells and rare tumor cells as well as mass-limited samples. In turn, it will be greatly beneficial to current biomedical research and systems biology.

cLC-SRM is a convenient targeted proteomics method that enables accurate multiplexed protein analysis of small numbers of cells including single cells. This method capitalizes on protein carrier-assisted one-pot sample preparation, in which all steps including cell collection, multistep cell lysis and digestion, transfer of peptide digests to capillary LC column for MS analysis, are performed in one pot (e.g., single tube or single well) ( Figure 1 ). This ‘all-in-one’ low-volume one-pot processing effectively maximizes the recovery of small numbers of cells for targeted proteomics analysis by greatly reducing possible surface absorption losses. There are two critical steps for cLC-SRM analysis: 1) after FACS sorting, immediate centrifugation is required to ensure that the collected cells are at the bottom of tubes or wells because low volume (~15 µL) is used to process small numbers of cells; 2) prior to the addition of trypsin for digestion, the TFE levels need to be reduced down to ≤10% for effective digestion. To avoid drying out samples resulting in unrecoverable loss, frequently checking the sample volume (~4 µL of the remaining volume) is suggested during Speed Vac concentrating. One-pot sample preparation can be further simplified by removal of reduction and alkylation steps with neglectable effect on digestion efficiency. One drawback is that cysteine containing peptides cannot be selected as surrogate peptides for target proteins. To avoid Speed Vac concentrating step for TFE removal we consider replacing TFE with MS-compatible surfactants (e.g., DDM: n-Dodecyl β-D-maltoside) for cell lysis because frequent checking sample volume severely prevents automation of sample processing with low throughput. This was evidenced by our recent data for DDM-assisted global single-cell proteomics analysis (unpublished). In addition, single carrier protein (e.g., BSA) may not be sufficient to unbiasedly reduce surface adsorption losses for every protein. This was evidenced by a few undetected proteins at >30,000 copies per cell (e.g., MAP2K1) in 10 MCF7 cells that should have been detected [30]. steps.title: Coat PCR Tubes
steps.instruction: Coat the surface of PCR tubes using nonhuman cell lysate digests.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL of nonhuman (e.g., Shewanella oneidensis) cell lysate digests at 0.2 µg/µL to PCR tubes.
Incubate at room temperature overnight.
Remove the cell lysate digests by pipetting.
Rinse PCR tubes 3 times with HPLC-grade water.
Airdry PCR tubes in a fume hood.
Store coated PCR tubes in a 4 °C freezer until use.

steps.title: Align and Verify FACS Machine
steps.instruction: Align the fluorescence-activated cell sorter (FACS) (e.g., BD Influx flow cytometer) into a 96-well PCR plate.

substeps.instruction: Use fluorescent beads with dyes excited by the laser source to provide reference signals.
Set the sort stream angle to the minimum possible to ensure cells land at the bottom of the wells.
Verify alignment by sorting ~100 droplets of PBS buffer onto an empty plate; recalibrate if droplets do not land on the bottom.

steps.title: Sort and Collect Cells
steps.instruction: Sort human breast cells into the prepared tubes and stabilize them.

substeps.instruction: Place coated PCR tubes into a 96-well PCR tube rack.
Sort desired numbers of human breast cells (MCF7 or MCF10A) into the precoated PCR tubes.
Immediately centrifuge sorted cells at 100 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Store sorted cells in a -80 °C freezer until further analysis.

steps.title: Add Carrier, Standards, and TFE
steps.instruction: Add reagents to the sample tubes for protein stabilization and standardization.

substeps.instruction: Add 4 µL of 25 mM NH4HCO3.
Add 1 µL of 10 ng/µL bovine serum albumin (BSA) in 25 mM NH4HCO3.
Add 0.3 µL of 100 fmol/µL crude heavy peptide standards (total 30 fmol), ensuring the tip is dispensed into the middle of the solution with no leftover liquid.
Add 9 µL of 100% TFE to reach a final concentration of ~60% TFE.
Centrifuge at 1500 x g for 5 min, then gently vortex at 100 x g for 3 min.

steps.title: Cell Lysis and Protein Denaturation
steps.instruction: Lysis and denature the proteins using sonication and heat.

substeps.instruction: Sonicate cells on ice for 1 min with 1-min intervals for 5 cycles (amplitude 70%, 0.5 Hz).
Incubate samples at 90 °C for 1 h using a PCR thermocycler with the heated-lid option.
Cool samples to room temperature via centrifugation at 1500 g for 3 min.

steps.title: Protein Reduction
steps.instruction: Reduce proteins using freshly prepared DTT.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 50 mM DTT: Dissolve 77.5 mg DTT in 1 mL 25 mM NH4HCO3 (500 mM), then add 10 µL of this to 90 µL 25 mM NH4HCO3.
Add 0.6 µL of the 50 mM DTT to the sample (final concentration 2 mM).
Centrifuge at 1500 g for 5 min, then gently mix at 850 rpm for 3 min.
Incubate at 56 °C for 1 h with gentle shaking at 100 g.
Cool to room temperature and centrifuge at 1500 g for 3 min.

steps.title: Protein Alkylation
steps.instruction: Alkylate proteins using freshly prepared IAA.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 60 mM IAA: Dissolve 74.3 mg IAA in 1 mL 25 mM NH4HCO3 (400 mM), then add 15 µL of this to 85 µL 25 mM NH4HCO3.
Add 0.5 µL of 60 mM IAA to the tube (final concentration ~2 mM).
Incubate in the dark at room temperature for 30 min with gentle shaking at 100 g.

steps.title: TFE Removal and Trypsin Digestion
steps.instruction: Concentrate the sample and perform enzymatic digestion.

substeps.instruction: Reduce sample volume to ~4 µL using a Speed Vac concentrator to remove TFE.
Add 9 µL of 25 mM NH4HCO3 and 1-3 µL of 15 ng/µL trypsin (final trypsin concentration 1-3 ng/µL).
Mix gently at 100 g for 3 min and incubate overnight (~16 hours) at 37 °C.
Add 0.5 µL of 5% formic acid to stop the reaction.
Centrifuge for 1 h at 1500 g.
Store in -80 °C freezer or 4 °C freezer for immediate analysis.

steps.title: LC-SRM Sample Preparation
steps.instruction: Transfer processed samples into LC vials.

substeps.instruction: Remove the cap of the PCR tube.
Insert the PCR tube into an LC vial and close it.
Alternatively, for 96-well plates, use a mat cover to seal the plate for direct analysis.

steps.title: UPLC-QQQ MS Analysis
steps.instruction: Perform LC-SRM analysis using UPLC coupled to a triple quadrupole mass spectrometer.

substeps.instruction: Connect capillary C18 columns (75 µm i.d. × 20 cm for standard or 100 µm i.d. × 10 cm for short gradient) to a 20 μm i.d. fused silica electrospray emitter via a stainless metal union.
Use a 20 µL sample loop to load the entire sample (~15 µL).
Set mobile phase A to 0.1% formic acid in water and mobile phase B to 0.1% formic acid in 90% acetonitrile.

For >10 target proteins (Standard Gradient): Flow rate 300 nL/min; 5-20% B (26 min), 20-25% B (10 min), 25-40% B (8 min), 40-95% B (1 min), 95% B (7 min), re-equilibrate at 99.5% A (8 min). Total: 52 min.
For ≤10 target proteins (Short Gradient): Flow rate 400 nL/min; 5-95% B in 5 min, re-equilibrate at 99.5% A for 5 min. Total: 10 min.
Set QQQ MS parameters: Ion spray voltage 2,400 ± 100 V, capillary offset 35 V, skimmer offset -5 V, capillary inlet temperature 220 °C, and other parameters via automatic tuning.

steps.title: SRM Method Optimization and Quantification
steps.instruction: Determine retention times and quantify target proteins.

substeps.instruction: Spike various concentrations of crude heavy peptide standards into 20-50 ng/µL nonhuman cell lysate digests to determine retention time (RT) and interference transitions.
Use RT scheduled SRM mode with a scan window ≥6 min and total cycle time of 1 s (minimum dwell time 10 ms per transition).
Import raw data into Skyline software for visualization.
Identify peaks based on: 1) same LC retention time, and 2) similar relative peak intensity ratios between endogenous (light) and isotope-labeled (heavy) peptides.
Manually inspect SRM data for correct peak assignment and boundaries.
Quantify proteins using the best transition (high signal, no matrix interference) and use others as references.
Calculate S/N ratio (peak apex intensity / average background noise within ±15 s for standard or ±6 s for short gradient).
Define LOD (S/N ≥ 3) and LOQ (S/N ≥ 7 and surrogate peptide response within linear dynamic range).
Use multiple replicates to determine SD and CV.
